evidence.claim: The five nuclear-weapon states said a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, that nuclear weapons should serve defensive purposes, and that none of their nuclear weapons are targeted at each other or at any other state.
evidence.title: JOINT STATEMENT Of the Leaders of the Five Nuclear-Weapon States On Preventing Nuclear War and Avoiding Arms Races
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: The five nuclear-weapon states said a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, that nuclear weapons should serve defensive purposes, and that none of their nuclear weapons are targeted at each other or at any other state.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous government text for the five-power statement.
evidence.period_fit: Strong 2022 fit; this is the central public non-escalation statement Xi's China joined.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct at the level of Chinese head-of-state/party leadership; the statement is joint and system-level.
contrary_evidence: The statement is declaratory and does not itself show later restraint in force structure or crisis behavior.

evidence.claim: China called for continued strategic-stability communication and in-depth dialogue on reducing the role of nuclear weapons in national security doctrines, including on missile defense, outer space, cyberspace, and artificial intelligence.
evidence.title: Upholding the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons for World Peace and Development
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: China called for continued strategic-stability communication and in-depth dialogue on reducing the role of nuclear weapons in national security doctrines, including on missile defense, outer space, cyberspace, and artificial intelligence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official NPT review-cycle statement with specific policy asks and issue areas.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 NPT review diplomacy and highly relevant to the year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong system-level attribution under Xi's leadership; this is China's stated line in 2022.
contrary_evidence: The statement advocates restraint rhetorically, but does not prove implementation.
It also frames responsibility as something others, especially the U.S., must meet first.

evidence.claim: In response to the Pentagon's forecast, Zhao Lijian said China follows a self-defensive nuclear strategy, sticks to no-first-use, exercises utmost restraint, keeps capabilities at the minimum level required by national security, and is never part of any arms race.
evidence.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Zhao Lijian's Regular Press Conference on November 30, 2022
evidence.publisher: Embassy of the People's Republic of China in the Republic of Ireland
evidence.excerpt: In response to the Pentagon's forecast, Zhao Lijian said China follows a self-defensive nuclear strategy, sticks to no-first-use, exercises utmost restraint, keeps capabilities at the minimum level required by national security, and is never part of any arms race.
evidence.source_locator: Q&A response to AFP on the Pentagon report
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Chinese government response, but it is advocacy and self-description rather than independent verification.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2022 contemporaneous response to the U.S. report on China's buildup.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect, but directly tied to the Xi-led state's nuclear posture claim.
contrary_evidence: This is self-justification and may understate the pace of modernization.
It does not address the 2022 silo-field buildup.

evidence.claim: China halted senior-level military dialogue with the United States and cancelled a maritime military-security meeting after Pelosi's Taiwan visit, a move Reuters said raised the risk of accidental escalation at a critical moment.
evidence.title: China halts high-level military dialogue with U.S., suspends other cooperation
evidence.excerpt: China halted senior-level military dialogue with the United States and cancelled a maritime military-security meeting after Pelosi's Taiwan visit, a move Reuters said raised the risk of accidental escalation at a critical moment.
evidence.source_locator: lead and lines 418-420 in the article mirror
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is timely and specific, though republished on a financial-news site.
evidence.period_fit: Excellent fit for the August 2022 Taiwan crisis and crisis-communication lens.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Xi's system-level crisis management choice, though the press statement was issued by the foreign ministry.
contrary_evidence: Beijing framed the move as retaliation for Pelosi's visit, not as a communications risk.
The article does not show whether backchannels remained open.

evidence.claim: The white paper states that peaceful reunification is the first choice and that use of force would be the last resort under compelling circumstances.
evidence.title: Full Text: The Taiwan Question and China's Reunification in the New Era
evidence.excerpt: The white paper states that peaceful reunification is the first choice and that use of force would be the last resort under compelling circumstances.
evidence.source_locator: white paper text and the Aug. 17 press conference explanation
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official PRC white paper and accompanying explanation of its policy line.
evidence.period_fit: Directly contemporaneous to the August 2022 Taiwan escalation period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong; this is the policy line of the Xi-led state and party.
contrary_evidence: The same document also insists reunification cannot be halted and rejects Taiwan independence.
That combination keeps coercive risk high despite the peace-first framing.

evidence.claim: Xi said the Bali meeting should stabilize China-U.S. ties, improve world peace and stability, and put the relationship back on a healthy and steady track.
evidence.title: Xi Jinping: Put China-U.S. relationship on the right course and bring it back to the track of healthy and stable growth
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: Xi said the Bali meeting should stabilize China-U.S. ties, improve world peace and stability, and put the relationship back on a healthy and steady track.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential readout from the Chinese foreign ministry with exact dating and attribution.
evidence.period_fit: Excellent fit for late-2022 diplomatic crisis management and bilateral de-escalation.
contrary_evidence: This is a diplomatic aspiration, not proof of durable restraint or changed conduct.
The same period still included Taiwan coercion and military signaling.

evidence.claim: Xi and Putin held extensive talks on international strategic security and said their coordination would help maintain world strategic security and stability.
evidence.title: President Xi Jinping Held Talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: Xi and Putin held extensive talks on international strategic security and said their coordination would help maintain world strategic security and stability.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official readout of the Xi-Putin summit and joint line on strategic security.
evidence.period_fit: Strong fit for the inherited strategic posture at the start of 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct for Xi's diplomatic choice to deepen strategic coordination with Russia.
contrary_evidence: This is not a peace settlement and it predates Russia's full-scale invasion by weeks.
The language is broad and strategic, not a concrete conflict-de-escalation measure.

evidence.claim: Xi said China and Russia would continue supporting each other on core sovereignty and security interests and deepen strategic coordination in the UN and other forums.
evidence.title: Xi talks with Putin over phone
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: Xi said China and Russia would continue supporting each other on core sovereignty and security interests and deepen strategic coordination in the UN and other forums.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official readout of a head-of-state call with explicit strategic commitments.
evidence.period_fit: Excellent fit for mid-2022 external posture.
contrary_evidence: This supports alignment with Russia more than peace restraint.
It does not show any Chinese effort to distance itself from the invasion of Ukraine.

evidence.claim: China urged restraint, direct Russia-Ukraine dialogue, and support for a peaceful settlement while saying civilians should be protected from a worsening crisis.
evidence.title: Wang Yi Expounds China's Five-Point Position on the Current Ukraine Issue
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: China urged restraint, direct Russia-Ukraine dialogue, and support for a peaceful settlement while saying civilians should be protected from a worsening crisis.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous foreign-ministry statement with explicit policy points.
evidence.period_fit: Very strong fit for the first days after Russia's full-scale invasion.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong system-level attribution under Xi's leadership.
contrary_evidence: The statement also echoed Russian security grievances and did not condemn the invasion.
That makes it qualified restraint, not principled opposition to aggression.

evidence.claim: China called for renewed dialogue, restraint, civilian protection, safeguards for nuclear facilities, and mediation to promote a political settlement in Ukraine.
evidence.title: Wang Yi Attends UN Security Council Foreign Ministers' Meeting on Ukraine Issue
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: China called for renewed dialogue, restraint, civilian protection, safeguards for nuclear facilities, and mediation to promote a political settlement in Ukraine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct UN-side statement with concrete de-escalatory and humanitarian language.
evidence.period_fit: Excellent fit for September 2022 international crisis diplomacy.
contrary_evidence: The statement also blames unilateral sanctions and does not criticize Russian aggression explicitly.
It is still declaratory rather than an operational peace action.

evidence.claim: The Party's Taiwan office said Pelosi's visit seriously infringed China's sovereignty, violated the one-China principle, and sent a wrong signal to Taiwan independence forces.
evidence.title: Taiwan Work Office of CPC Central Committee issues statement on Pelosi's visit to Taiwan
evidence.excerpt: The Party's Taiwan office said Pelosi's visit seriously infringed China's sovereignty, violated the one-China principle, and sent a wrong signal to Taiwan independence forces.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct Chinese party-state statement on the trigger for the Taiwan crisis.
evidence.period_fit: Exact fit for the August 2022 Taiwan escalation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct as a statement of the Xi-led party-state position.
contrary_evidence: This is justification, not neutral evidence of necessity.
It frames escalation as defensive even though outside observers saw it as coercive.

evidence.claim: China said the Taiwan drills were necessary and legitimate, and that safety alerts and navigation warnings were issued before they began.
evidence.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Hua Chunying’s Regular Press Conference on August 3, 2022
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: China said the Taiwan drills were necessary and legitimate, and that safety alerts and navigation warnings were issued before they began.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official explanation with a concrete safety-precaution claim, but still self-justifying.
evidence.period_fit: Directly contemporaneous to the Taiwan drill cycle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant to Xi's system-level crisis posture.
contrary_evidence: The same passage says the drills were a way to 'speak' to adversaries, which sounds coercive.
Independent reporting described blockade-like effects and high escalation risk.

evidence.claim: China suspended senior military dialogue and canceled a maritime military-security meeting with the United States after Pelosi's Taiwan visit.
evidence.title: China halts high-level military dialogue with U.S., suspends other cooperation
evidence.excerpt: China suspended senior military dialogue and canceled a maritime military-security meeting with the United States after Pelosi's Taiwan visit.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is strong for contemporaneous event reporting, though this is a republished copy.
evidence.period_fit: Excellent fit for crisis communication and de-escalation analysis in August 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Xi's system-level decision to harden the crisis response.
contrary_evidence: Beijing framed this as retaliation for Pelosi's visit.
The move reduced crisis communication channels at a tense moment.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that China launched large-scale drills after Pelosi's visit, with some planned within Taiwan's 12-nautical-mile territory and described by Taiwanese officials as blockade-like.
evidence.title: Taiwan full of praise, support for Taiwan during visit that infuriated China
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that China launched large-scale drills after Pelosi's visit, with some planned within Taiwan's 12-nautical-mile territory and described by Taiwanese officials as blockade-like.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting provides timely independent corroboration of the escalation context.
evidence.period_fit: Excellent fit for the core August 2022 Taiwan coercion episode.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct as state conduct under Xi's authority.
contrary_evidence: China said the exercises were defensive and lawful.
The reporting relies in part on Taiwanese officials' characterization of the drills.

evidence.claim: China said it would settle South China Sea disputes through negotiation and consultation, implement the DOC, and maintain peace and stability at sea.
evidence.title: China Stays Committed to Peace, Stability and Order in The South China Sea
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: China said it would settle South China Sea disputes through negotiation and consultation, implement the DOC, and maintain peace and stability at sea.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct position paper with detailed maritime policy language.
evidence.period_fit: Good fit for 2022 maritime policy and law framing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but important system-level posture under Xi.
contrary_evidence: This is a declaratory position paper, not proof of on-water restraint.
The same document rejects the U.S. legal reading and maintains expansive Chinese claims.

evidence.claim: ASEAN and China reaffirmed peaceful dispute settlement, freedom of navigation, self-restraint, and avoidance of force in the South China Sea.
evidence.title: Joint Statement on the 20th Anniversary of the Declaration on the Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: ASEAN and China reaffirmed peaceful dispute settlement, freedom of navigation, self-restraint, and avoidance of force in the South China Sea.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official joint statement with explicit commitments and dated adoption.
evidence.period_fit: Excellent fit for late-2022 regional diplomacy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant to Xi's state-led regional posture.
contrary_evidence: Joint statements do not guarantee compliance on the water.
China continued coercive maritime behavior elsewhere in the same year.

evidence.claim: The Philippine coast guard said a Chinese coast guard vessel maneuvered so closely that it constrained a Philippine patrol ship near Scarborough Shoal.
evidence.title: Philippines slams Chinese coastguard’s 'close distance manoeuvring' at Scarborough Shoal
evidence.publisher: Reuters via South China Morning Post
evidence.excerpt: The Philippine coast guard said a Chinese coast guard vessel maneuvered so closely that it constrained a Philippine patrol ship near Scarborough Shoal.
evidence.source_locator: reporting summary and quoted coast guard description
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting summarized by SCMP; timely but based on Philippine statements.
evidence.period_fit: Strong 2022 fit for South China Sea coercive behavior.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct as conduct by Chinese maritime forces under Xi's national-security authority.
contrary_evidence: China typically claims such actions are lawful enforcement in its own waters.
This is one incident, not the full year-long pattern.

evidence.claim: Indian and Chinese troops clashed in Tawang on December 9, causing minor injuries on both sides and prompting immediate disengagement.
evidence.title: Indian, Chinese troops suffer minor injuries in clash on Dec 9: Indian army
evidence.excerpt: Indian and Chinese troops clashed in Tawang on December 9, causing minor injuries on both sides and prompting immediate disengagement.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraph and quoted army statement
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting of a concrete border clash with clear attribution from the Indian army.
evidence.period_fit: Exact late-2022 fit for the India-China border exposure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct as a cross-border military incident under Xi's command authority.
contrary_evidence: The clash did not escalate into a wider war.
Both sides disengaged, and Chinese officials did not publicly escalate further.
